messages:
Maya - Support: Hey team, escalation from AcmeApp — they say during short bursts (500–1k reqs over ~30s) they see lots of perceived throttling: 429s and big latency tail spikes. They use continuous batching + KV cache for conversation state. Posting trimmed logs and repro steps from the customer below.

AcmeApp (customer): Hi, hitting 429s around the same time our KV cache is warming. Timeline: start burst -> KV hit rate low -> latency jumps -> 429s start ~10s into burst. We are on hosted API, model: rwd-llama-70b-q4. Our token sizes are small (~15 tokens). Example curl: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXX' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-70b-q4","input":"hi","stream":false}'
```
Response snippet: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{ "error": { "type":"rate_limited", "message":"burst capacity exceeded" } }
```
We also see header: `x-burst-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 12` on 429s.

Maya - Support: They provided request ids: req=rx5a3, rx5a4, rx5b7. Attached small sample of runtime logs they copied: ```
[2026-10-18T14:05:12Z] req=rx5a3 queue_len=82 batch_wait_ms=23 kv_cache_hit=false exec_time_ms=1900 result=429
[2026-10-18T14:05:12Z] req=rx5a4 queue_len=90 batch_wait_ms=28 kv_cache_hit=true exec_time_ms=210 result=200
[2026-10-18T14:05:13Z] req=rx5b7 queue_len=110 batch_wait_ms=46 kv_cache_hit=false exec_time_ms=2300 result=429
```

Ravi - Oncall: thanks Maya. Quick qs: is this limited to that model/region? Also did they route traffic through any special routing policy? Can you paste the API key prefix and region (we just need region).

AcmeApp (customer): Region: us-west-2. Key prefix: rw_cust_7. No special routing. We saw the spike right after a deploy on our side but the pattern repeats on multiple bursts.

Jun - Runtime: preliminary theory: continuous batching holds requests up to batching_window_ms to aggregate. Under heavy bursts and when KV cache cold, many requests become full generation (hot path) which increases token compute on GPU. That increases per-batch exec_time and reduces throughput. The fronting quota/burst-protection layer is configured to protect multi-tenant capacity — when the internal in-flight tokens or queue_length exceeds thresholds we surface 429s rather than letting queue grow unbounded. That matches queue_len ~110 in the logs. So customers see 429s during cold-KV bursts because of combined effects: (1) cold KV -> more tokens, (2) batching_window + long exec_time -> increasing queue wait -> front-end burst guard -> 429s.

Leah - ML: also check that KV cache keying isn't too granular — if each request has a unique conversation key it prevents cache hits. With many unique keys cold cache churns the cache and reduces hit rate.

Jun - Runtime: repro plan for us: run synthetic driver that simulates their burst profile (1k requests over 30s, 15 token avg) with both kv warm and kv cold. I can run on staging with identical runtime config (batching_window_ms=25, max_batch_size=64, per-customer concurrency quota=12). Expectation: with kv_cache_hit=false spike exec_time crosses SLO and queue_len triggers quota-reject path.

Maya - Support: customer asked for mitigations now. They want quick mitigations they can do on their side while we investigate. Options they listed: reduce concurrency, add jitter, pre-warm cache with a warmup endpoint, or switch to a smaller model. Any recommendations?

Jun - Runtime: short-term recommendations for customer: 1) pre-warm KV cache: replay typical conversation prefixes just before bursts (10–20 warmup reqs) 2) lower client-side burst concurrency (throttle to ~50–60 rps instead of 100–200) 3) increase batching_window_ms slightly (e.g., 35ms) to improve batching efficiency but only if they can tolerate slight added latency 4) if they have a dedicated reservation, move to Dedicated/Dedicated-burst tier. Also we'll consider bumping their per-customer burst quota temporarily.

AcmeApp (customer): We can try pre-warm and lower concurrency. Can you also explain why kv_cache_hit=true lines still had some 200s but we still saw 429s around them?

Jun - Runtime: good catch — KV hits reduce compute but don't eliminate GPU synchronizations and shared resources. A mix of hit and miss can still cause queue backs, especially if misses have much larger exec_time. So intermittent hits won't prevent the overall queue from filling if misses dominate. Also note batching semantics: a batch containing a mix of hits+misses might wait until the slowest request finishes (depending on runtime implementation) which can increase tail latency.

Leah - ML: for longer term: we can add a small fast-path for pure-KV-hit responses that can be served without full GPU pass (a pure KV lookup + response assembly). That would reduce pressure on GPU for high-cache-hit workloads. Filing an RFC.

Jun - Runtime: infra ask: Ops/Oncall — can you expose metrics for this customer for last month: per-minute queue_len, batch_wait_ms_p50/p95, kv_cache_hit_rate, inflight_tokens, and burst_reject_count? Ravi, can you also check if any config change (global or per-tenant) happened near the customer's first incident timestamp?

Ravi - Oncall: Roger. I’ll pull cluster metrics and per-tenant counters (x-burst-remaining, x-burst-reset) and check deploy log near 14:00 UTC. If quota bump is needed we can do a targeted increase for rw_cust_7.

Maya - Support: customer wants repro steps so they can test mitigations. Jun suggested a local load test. Here's a simple bash loop they can run to simulate: ```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-70b-q4","input":"hi","stream":false}' &
  if (( i % 200 == 0 )); then sleep 0.5; fi
done
wait
```
Add a tiny random sleep (0-10ms) to simulate jitter. Also to test cache warm: send 20 identical prefills before the burst.

AcmeApp (customer): Running warm + lower concurrency right now, will report back in ~30m. Thanks.

Jun - Runtime: I'll also instrument a short synthetic run from staging and post aggregate metrics: p50/p95/p99 of batch_wait_ms, exec_time_ms, kv_hit_rate, and rejects. If we can reproduce we'll propose either increasing their per-tenant burst budget or adjusting runtime to prefer KV-hit fast-paths.

Leah - ML: filing internal ticket to evaluate fast-paths and KV eviction patterns. cc:@deploy-bot to track the ticket id once created.

Deploy Bot: Ticket RWD-5632 created: "KV-hit fast-path evaluation for burst-heavy customers" — assigned to Leah, priority P2.

Ravi - Oncall: Update: I see a spike in deploys from a deploy-job exactly 6 minutes before the first reported incident in the customer logs, but it was a customer-side deploy. No infra changes on our side. I’m going to run a per-tenant quota increase to rw_cust_7 for the next 24h to reduce user-impact while we investigate.

Maya - Support: thanks all. Action items: 1) Acme to test warm+concurrency changes and report. 2) Ravi to apply temporary quota bump and gather metrics. 3) Jun to run staging repro and post graphs. 4) Leah to triage KV fast-path ticket. I’ll follow up with the customer after they report results. :thumbsup:

AcmeApp (customer): Confirmed — we see reduced 429s after warm + throttle. Will keep monitoring and share numbers tomorrow. Thanks everyone.
